recommendedTextbook.title: Essential Commerce for Senior Secondary Schools
recommendedTextbook.author: O. A. Longe
recommendedTextbook.approvedBy: NERDC & Lagos State Ministry of Basic Education

topics.topic: Introduction to Commerce and Historical Development in Nigeria
subtopics: Definition and scope of Commerce (Trade and Aids to Trade)
Historical evolution: Barter system, introduction of commodity money (cowries, manillas), modern fiat currency
Factors that accelerated commercial development in Nigeria (railways, banking, telecommunications, oil boom)
objectives: Define commerce and illustrate its comprehensive tree diagram
Analyze difficulties of trade by barter (double coincidence of wants)
Explain how modern fintech and digital banking have revolutionized Nigerian commerce

subtopics: Meaning of occupation: Industrial, commercial, service occupations
Stages of production: Primary (extraction), secondary (manufacturing/construction), tertiary (distribution/services)
Direct vs indirect services (doctors, teachers, civil servants, security)
objectives: Classify 15 Nigerian jobs into industrial, commercial, and service occupations
Differentiate extractive from manufacturing industries in Nigeria
Explain why production is incomplete until goods reach the final consumer

topics.topic: Home Trade: Wholesaling and Channels of Distribution
subtopics: Wholesale trade: Characteristics, types of wholesalers (merchant, general, specialist, cash-and-carry)
Functions of wholesalers to manufacturers (financing, warehousing, bulk breaking, market feedback)
Arguments for and against the elimination of the middleman in Nigeria
objectives: Analyze 5 essential services provided by wholesalers in Nigerian supply chains
Evaluate economic conditions under which a manufacturer may bypass wholesalers
Explain the concept of bulk breaking in traditional commodity markets like Bodija and Alaba

subtopics: Small-scale retailing: Hawkers, mobile shops, kiosks, tied shops, market stalls
Large-scale retailing: Department stores, supermarkets, hypermarkets, chain stores, mail order
E-commerce and online retail in Nigeria (Jumia, Konga, social commerce via WhatsApp and Instagram)
objectives: Compare advantages and disadvantages of street hawking versus modern supermarkets
Identify 4 operational traits of department stores and multiple shops
Examine logistical and cyber-fraud challenges facing Nigerian e-commerce retailers
